title: US online shop, China-made kitchenware
subtitle: Silicone and bamboo kitchen tools by sea, as of 25 Mar 2025
text: I run an online shop in the US selling silicone and bamboo kitchen tool sets made in China, about 400 sets a week. A set sells for $28 and lands in my warehouse at about $12.50, including duty and freight. An order takes about 5 weeks to arrive by sea; I keep about 6 weeks of stock and could put about $25,000 into more. Other sellers on the same marketplaces charge about $27.

series.label: US extra duty on Chinese goods (fentanyl + reciprocal)

steps.text: The fentanyl-related duty on Chinese goods rose from 10% to 20%.
A 10% baseline tariff on all imports took effect, so Chinese goods paid 30% in total.
The country rate on China rose to 84% (executive order of April 8), for 104% in total.
The rate on China rose to 125% (executive order of April 9), for 145% in total.
After talks in Geneva the US cut the reciprocal rate on China to 10%, keeping the 20% fentanyl duty: 30% in total.

what_happened.text: The fentanyl-related duty on Chinese goods rose from 10% to 20%.
A 10% baseline tariff on all imports took effect, so Chinese goods paid 30% in total.
The country rate on China rose to 84% (executive order of April 8), for 104% in total.
The rate on China rose to 125% (executive order of April 9), for 145% in total.
After talks in Geneva the US cut the reciprocal rate on China to 10%, keeping the 20% fentanyl duty: 30% in total.
The US and China extended the pause on the higher reciprocal rates to November 10; the 30% total stayed.

caveats: The path is the extra duty by date, applied when goods enter the US: an order placed in week t pays the rate in force 5 weeks later. The cost rise is (1 + duty then) / (1 + 20% at the as-of date) − 1, on the part of the landed cost that scales with the duty (set at 86%: $9.00 of goods at $12.50 landed). The $9.00 goods cost, the $1.40 freight and the made-up shop are the owner's figures, not data.

Only the extra duties of this timeline are in the path. Section 301 duties (7.5% to 25% on many Chinese kitchenware lines, depending on the product code) were already in force and are not added; they would make the real rise a few points smaller. Steel and aluminium kitchenware faced separate Section 232 duties; this case is silicone and bamboo. Ending de minimis for China (May 2) does not touch bulk sea freight. No product exemption we found covered kitchenware.

Goods already on the water on 25 Mar that arrived after 9 Apr also paid the higher duty in real life; the engine charges that stock its old cost. Rivals face the same duty here (their cost moves too).
